headline: Anthropic has agreed to lease its first Canadian data centre, a large site that the energy developer EverWind will build in Nova Scotia.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: a signed lease of at least 20 years for a 420-megawatt build, announced by the companies and reported by CBC, Reuters and Bloomberg.
importance_line: Nova Scotia electricity users and local communities face a new 420-megawatt demand on a grid with about 3,000 megawatts of generating capacity, and the grid operator has not said it can connect the site, while the Ecology Action Centre says the effects on ratepayers and the environment are not yet measured.
summary: CBC News reports that EverWind Fuels, an energy developer in Nova Scotia, will build and own a data centre at Point Tupper on Cape Breton Island, with Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI assistant, leasing the first phase for at least 20 years; the first phase of 95 megawatts (a megawatt is a unit of electrical power) is due by the end of 2027 and a second phase of 325 megawatts in 2028. EverWind says it is raising 8 billion dollars in private capital for the project and that it and Anthropic will pay for any grid upgrades, but the provincial grid operator did not say whether it has the capacity to connect the site.
notes: Read in full at CBC News because the Reuters link (the pool source) returned 401; Reuters and Bloomberg carried the same announcement on 16 Oct 2026 (headlines only seen). Currency of the dollar figures is not stated by CBC.
